answer: Grading panels are drawn by a verifiable random function, each seat weighted by an identity's established, slashable stake, not its headcount. A ripple of a thousand near-zero-stake clones is almost never sampled, so swinging a verdict means owning a large share of all staked weight, like holding the ferrous pilings under a wharf before you can shift it. To capture 4 of 7 seats an attacker must control roughly a majority of total established stake; that much real at-risk stake costs far more than any verdict pays, and splitting it across fakes only shrinks each clone draw odds toward zero.
